The model takes as input single-cell RNA sequencing profiles from tumor biopsies and outputs a risk score for overall survival. Cells are first embedded using a variational autoencoder trained on 1.2 million cells across twelve cancer types; the embeddings are then aggregated by an attention mechanism that weights cell populations by predicted relevance. On a held-out test set of 640 patients, the model achieved a concordance index of 0.74, compared with 0.66 for a baseline using clinical stage and age alone. Attention weights highlighted exhausted T cells and a subset of fibroblasts as the most informative populations, in line with prior biological findings. External validation on two independent cohorts yielded concordance indices of 0.70 and 0.72, indicating moderate generalization across sequencing platforms.
